items.explanation: After w meaning "in" the noun takes the locative: Kraków → w Krakowie.
optionNotes: The nominative: after w the noun must change.
The genitive, used after do and z: do Krakowa.
The instrumental, used after z meaning "with".

items.explanation: Dom is an exception: it takes -u in the locative: w domu.
optionNotes: Most nouns take -e, but dom takes -u.
The nominative: after w the noun must change.
The instrumental, used after być for jobs and after z.

items.prompt: Czekam ___ przystanku. (I'm waiting at the stop.)
items.explanation: Przystanek is one of the na-places: na przystanku, na poczcie, na dworcu.
optionNotes: Most places take w, but przystanek takes na.
Do means "to" and takes the genitive.

items.prompt: Ania mieszka w ___. (Ania lives in Poland.)
items.explanation: Feminine -a → -e in the locative, and k changes to c: Polska → w Polsce.
optionNotes: The nominative: after w the noun must change.
The genitive, used after z and do: z Polski.
